$comment: Pages that violate CLAUDE.md's CSRF token bootstrapping rule TODAY.
THE DEFECT, in CLAUDE.md's own words: CSRFGuard's client script only injects
the hidden CSRF-TOKEN input into a <form> with a real action and a non-GET
method. A page that reads that input from an AJAX POST -- directly, or
through share/javascript/carlos-ajax.js, which reads it on the page's behalf
-- and carries no such form and no /WEB-INF/jspf/csrf-token.jspf include
sends an EMPTY token. The request is answered with an HTML error page, the
page's catch block swallows it, and the user is shown nothing at all.
WHY THESE ARE LISTED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE. They are defects in the
APPLICATION, not in the checks. This branch is test coverage; fixing a
bootstrap needs a browser to confirm the token actually populates (and, on a
page that sets its own script-src, a CSP nonce -- see CLAUDE.md). They are
recorded as finding 10 in docs/ui-tests/app-findings-log.md and tracked in
issue #3665.
HOW THEY WERE MISSED UNTIL NOW. The audit's applicability test required the
token read and the AJAX send to appear in the page's OWN source. All six of
these POST through CarlosAjax instead, so the audit classified them NOT
APPLICABLE and reported the whole webapp clean: 25 applicable pages, zero
violations. Widening applicability to the shared helper took it to 37
applicable pages and these six violations.
THIS FILE IS A BURN-DOWN, not a permission. csrf-bootstrap-audit.test.js
fails the build on any violation NOT listed here, and equally when a listed
file stops violating without being removed -- so the set can only shrink.
Delete an entry when its page is fixed.
